1.q: In spite the side effects, the new medicine is very popular.
a: In spite of the side effects, the new medicine is very popular.
Despite the side effects, the new medicine is very popular.

1.q: Many people are addicted on sugary drinks.
a: Many people are addicted to sugary drinks.

1.q: If the drug would be cheaper, more people could buy it.
a: If the drug were cheaper, more people could buy it.
If the drug was cheaper, more people could buy it.
1.why: Second conditional: "if" + past simple ("were/was"), never "if + would".

1.q: While the doctor ____ (explain) the results, my phone rang.
a: was explaining
1.why: The longer action in progress uses the past continuous; the short action that interrupts it uses the past simple.

1.q: I visited a nutritionist. Her advice changed my diet.
a: I visited a nutritionist whose advice changed my diet.
I visited a nutritionist, whose advice changed my diet.
1.why: "Whose" replaces a possessive (her, his, their) in a relative clause.

2.q: Poor countries should to get help to protect their forests.
a: Poor countries should get help to protect their forests.
2.why: Modal verbs (must, should, can) are followed by the base verb without "to".

2.q: There is less trees in the city centre than in the suburbs.
a: There are fewer trees in the city centre than in the suburbs.
2.why: Use "fewer" with plural countable nouns (trees) and "less" with uncountable ones (water, money).

2.q: The government has signed the agreement last year.
a: The government signed the agreement last year.
2.why: A finished time (last year, in 2015, yesterday) needs the past simple, not the present perfect.

2.q: Scientists ____ (study) this forest for over thirty years.
a: have studied
have been studying
2.why: An action that started in the past and continues now, with "for/since", uses the present perfect (simple or continuous).

2.q: Although the forest is protected, people still cut down trees.
a: Despite the forest being protected, people still cut down trees.
Despite being protected, the forest is still cut down by people.
Despite the protection of the forest, people still cut down trees.
2.why: "Despite" is followed by a noun or an -ing form, not a full clause with a subject and verb.

3.q: The police is looking for the people who damaged the park.
a: The police are looking for the people who damaged the park.

3.q: This is the first time I see so many birds in one place.
a: This is the first time I have seen so many birds in one place.
3.why: "It's / This is the first time" is followed by the present perfect.

3.q: The amount of wild animals in Europe are getting smaller.
a: The number of wild animals in Europe is getting smaller.
3.why: Use "number" with countable nouns (animals); "the number of …" takes a singular verb.

3.q: By 2050, cities ____ (grow) by another two billion people.
a: will have grown
3.why: The future perfect (will have + past participle) describes something completed before a time in the future.

3.q: There isn't enough green space in my city.
a: My city has too little green space.

4.q: My doctor made me to give up sugar.
a: My doctor made me give up sugar.
4.why: "Make someone do": no "to" after make (and let).

4.q: I recommend to start the day with a good breakfast.
a: I recommend starting the day with a good breakfast.
4.why: "Recommend" and "suggest" are followed by an -ing form, not "to" + verb.

4.q: We have eaten at that new vegetarian café last weekend.
a: We ate at that new vegetarian café last weekend.
4.why: A finished time (last weekend) needs the past simple.

4.q: If I ____ (have) a garden, I would grow my own vegetables.
a: had
4.why: Second conditional: "if" + past simple, then "would" + base verb.

4.q: You will feel more energetic if you eat more vegetables.
a: Eating more vegetables will make you feel more energetic.
Eating more vegetables makes you feel more energetic.
4.why: An -ing form (gerund) can be the subject of a sentence.

5.q: Warmer winters have a big affect on insects.
a: Warmer winters have a big effect on insects.
5.why: "Effect" is the noun; "affect" is the verb.

5.q: Mosquitoes are insects who can carry dangerous diseases.
a: Mosquitoes are insects which can carry dangerous diseases.
Mosquitoes are insects that can carry dangerous diseases.
5.why: Use "which/that" for animals and things, "who" for people.

5.q: The water isn't enough clean to drink.
a: The water isn't clean enough to drink.
5.why: "Enough" comes after an adjective (clean enough) but before a noun (enough water).

5.q: By the end of the century, many animals ____ (move) to colder areas.
a: will have moved
5.why: Future perfect: something completed before a future time.

5.q: Many animals are moving north. This means new diseases may spread.
5.start: Many animals are moving north, which
a: Many animals are moving north, which means new diseases may spread.
5.why: ", which" can refer to the whole previous idea, not just one noun.

6.q: I was very boring in the chemistry lesson today.
a: I was very bored in the chemistry lesson today.
6.why: "-ed" adjectives describe how you feel (bored); "-ing" adjectives describe what causes it (boring).

6.q: The experiment was a success, everyone was very happy.
a: The experiment was a success. Everyone was very happy.
The experiment was a success, and everyone was very happy.
The experiment was a success; everyone was very happy.
6.why: Two full sentences can't be joined with only a comma: use a full stop, a semicolon or a linking word.

6.q: The results must check carefully before they are published.
a: The results must be checked carefully before they are published.
6.why: Results don't check anything: they are checked. Modal passive = modal + be + past participle.

6.q: This method ____ (test) in many laboratories since 2010.
a: has been tested
6.why: Present perfect passive (has/have been + past participle) with "since".

6.q: You don't have to wear gloves for this experiment.
a: It isn't necessary to wear gloves for this experiment.
6.why: "Don't have to" = "it isn't necessary to" (there is no obligation).

7.q: The data show that each of the mice react to the light.
a: The data show that each of the mice reacts to the light.
7.why: "Each of" + plural noun takes a singular verb.

7.q: The scientist succeeded to control the neurons with light.
a: The scientist succeeded in controlling the neurons with light.

7.q: If they had used more mice, the results would be more reliable last year.
a: If they had used more mice, the results would have been more reliable last year.
7.why: Third conditional (past): "if" + past perfect, then "would have" + past participle.

7.q: The mice ____ (train) to find food before the experiment started.
a: had been trained
were trained
7.why: Passive: the mice didn't train themselves. Past perfect passive shows it happened before another past action.

7.q: People believe that the brain controls every movement.
a: The brain is believed to control every movement.
7.why: Impersonal passive: "It is believed that X …" = "X is believed to …".

8.q: Robots can give us many advices about money.
a: Robots can give us a lot of advice about money.
Robots can give us much advice about money.
Robots can give us lots of advice about money.
8.why: "Advice" is uncountable: no plural, and use "a lot of/much", not "many".

8.q: I first used a chatbot two years before.
a: I first used a chatbot two years ago.
8.why: Counting back from now uses "ago"; "before" counts back from another past time.

8.q: AI not only writes texts but also it draws pictures.
a: AI not only writes texts but also draws pictures.
8.why: In "not only … but also", both parts must have the same form: "writes … draws".

8.q: When the new system arrived, the company ____ (already/train) its staff.
a: had already trained
8.why: Past perfect: an action completed before another past action.

8.q: Robots can sort parcels. They can do it day and night.
a: Robots can sort parcels day and night.
8.why: When two sentences share the same subject and verb, combine them and keep only the new information.

9.q: Yesterday I buyed vegetables at the market.
a: Yesterday I bought vegetables at the market.

9.q: The insects was kept in small boxes.
a: The insects were kept in small boxes.

9.q: This diet is more easier to follow than the last one.
a: This diet is easier to follow than the last one.
9.why: Don't use "more" with a comparative that already ends in -er.

9.q: If you ____ (skip) breakfast, you will feel hungry by ten o'clock.
a: skip
9.why: First conditional: "if" + present simple, "will" + base verb.

9.q: Cooking for ten people was very tiring for me.
a: I found cooking for ten people very tiring.
9.why: "I found something + adjective" gives your opinion of an experience.

10.q: Parents are afraid of their children to get sick at school.
a: Parents are afraid of their children getting sick at school.
10.why: After a preposition (of, about), use an -ing form, not "to" + verb.

10.q: Yesterday I must stay at home because I was ill.
a: Yesterday I had to stay at home because I was ill.
10.why: "Must" has no past form: use "had to".

10.q: One in five adults have high blood pressure.
a: One in five adults has high blood pressure.
10.why: "One in five …" takes a singular verb.

10.q: When I got to the clinic, the doctor ____ (go) home.
a: had gone
had already gone
10.why: Past perfect: the doctor left before I arrived.

10.q: She didn't check her blood sugar, so she felt ill.
a: If she had checked her blood sugar, she wouldn't have felt ill.
If she had checked her blood sugar, she would not have felt ill.
10.why: Third conditional imagines a different past: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

11.q: I read some interesting informations about fake news.
a: I read some interesting information about fake news.

11.q: The app doesn't let users to delete old posts.
a: The app doesn't let users delete old posts.

11.q: Many people believe fake news because of it looks real.
a: Many people believe fake news because it looks real.
Many people believe fake news because of how real it looks.

11.q: The platform ____ (remove) thousands of fake accounts last month.
a: removed
11.why: A finished time (last month) → past simple.

11.q: People share false stories. The stories make them angry.
a: People share false stories because the stories make them angry.
People share false stories because they make them angry.
11.why: "Because" joins a result to its reason.

12.q: The scientists found a rock, it came from Mars.
a: The scientists found a rock which came from Mars.
The scientists found a rock that came from Mars.
The scientists found a rock, which came from Mars.
12.why: A comma can't join two sentences: use a relative pronoun (which/that) or a full stop.

12.q: I study English since I was ten.
a: I have studied English since I was ten.
I have been studying English since I was ten.
12.why: From a past point until now (since/for) → present perfect.

12.q: Did you found the keys you lost?
a: Did you find the keys you lost?

12.q: The meteorite ____ (fall) in Antarctica thousands of years ago.
a: fell

12.q: Nobody has ever seen this kind of meteorite before.
a: This kind of meteorite has never been seen before.
12.why: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle.

13.q: The summers are getting hotter, don't it?
a: The summers are getting hotter, aren't they?
13.why: A question tag repeats the auxiliary of the sentence (are → aren't) and uses a pronoun (they).

13.q: This is the park where I go running in.
a: This is the park where I go running.
This is the park which I go running in.
13.why: "Where" already means "in which", so don't add "in" at the end.

13.q: The ice is melting more quick than scientists expected.
a: The ice is melting more quickly than scientists expected.
The ice is melting faster than scientists expected.
13.why: Verbs are described by adverbs: "more quickly" (or "faster").

13.q: Since 1980, each decade ____ (be) warmer than the one before.
a: has been

13.q: Summers will be even hotter. Many scientists think so.
a: Many scientists think that summers will be even hotter.

14.q: Most people guess wrong, even they read the statistics.
a: Most people guess wrong, even if they read the statistics.
Most people guess wrong, even when they read the statistics.
Most people guess wrong even if they read the statistics.
14.why: "Even" alone can't join two clauses: use "even if", "even when" or "even though".

14.q: My grandfather, that is 80, still works in his garden.
a: My grandfather, who is 80, still works in his garden.

14.q: Our neighbours are very friendly, they often invite us for tea.
a: Our neighbours are very friendly. They often invite us for tea.
Our neighbours are very friendly, and they often invite us for tea.
Our neighbours are very friendly; they often invite us for tea.
14.why: Don't join two sentences with only a comma.

14.q: Before the survey, the volunteers ____ (give) a short questionnaire.
a: were given
had been given
14.why: Passive: someone gave the volunteers a questionnaire.

14.q: The results surprised most of the researchers.
a: Most of the researchers were surprised by the results.
14.why: Active → passive: the object becomes the subject + be + past participle + by.

15.q: It takes a lot of energy for recycling plastic.
a: It takes a lot of energy to recycle plastic.

15.q: Every country have to reduce its plastic waste.
a: Every country has to reduce its plastic waste.

15.q: My aunt is a teacher in a small village, she loves her job.
a: My aunt is a teacher in a small village. She loves her job.
My aunt is a teacher in a small village, and she loves her job.
My aunt is a teacher in a small village; she loves her job.
15.why: Two sentences need a full stop, a semicolon or a linking word, not just a comma.

15.q: Only about 9% of all plastic ____ (recycle) so far.
a: has been recycled
15.why: "So far" → present perfect; plastic doesn't recycle itself → passive.

15.q: We use fewer plastic bags. The oceans will be cleaner.
a: If we use fewer plastic bags, the oceans will be cleaner.
15.why: First conditional for a real possibility: if + present, will + verb.

16.q: Everybody in my family like watching birds.
a: Everybody in my family likes watching birds.
16.why: "Everybody, nobody, somebody" take a singular verb.

16.q: It was a so loud song that it woke me up.
a: It was such a loud song that it woke me up.
The song was so loud that it woke me up.
16.why: "Such a + adjective + noun"; "so + adjective" (without a noun).

16.q: We were having dinner when the birds have started singing.
a: We were having dinner when the birds started singing.
16.why: A completed past action interrupting another one → past simple, not present perfect.

16.q: Researchers ____ (ignore) female birdsong for more than a century.
a: have ignored
16.why: "For more than a century" up to now → present perfect.

16.q: Scientists are interested in female birds' songs. This is new.
a: Scientists' interest in female birds' songs is new.
16.why: A verb phrase can become a noun phrase: "are interested in" → "interest in".

17.q: The noise makes impossible to sleep.
a: The noise makes it impossible to sleep.
17.why: "Make it + adjective + to + verb": the "it" is needed.

17.q: Bees are one of the most important insect on Earth.
a: Bees are one of the most important insects on Earth.
17.why: "One of the …" is followed by a plural noun.

17.q: If we had cleaner air, more bees will survive.
a: If we had cleaner air, more bees would survive.
17.why: Second conditional: if + past simple → "would", not "will".

17.q: Every year, millions of flowers ____ (pollinate) by bees.
a: are pollinated
17.why: Present simple passive: am/is/are + past participle.

17.q: Cities should ban old diesel cars.
a: Old diesel cars should be banned in cities.
Old diesel cars should be banned by cities.
17.why: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle.

18.q: The flight was cancelled due to snow fall heavily.
a: The flight was cancelled due to heavy snowfall.
The flight was cancelled due to heavy snow.
18.why: "Due to" is followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.

18.q: Can you explain me this word?
a: Can you explain this word to me?
18.why: "Explain something to someone", never "explain someone something".

18.q: Each of the patients take two tablets a day.
a: Each of the patients takes two tablets a day.

18.q: The new treatment ____ (test) on 200 patients last year.
a: was tested
18.why: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

18.q: The treatment is expensive. Many hospitals use it.
a: Although the treatment is expensive, many hospitals use it.
18.why: "Although" shows a contrast between two ideas.

19.q: Electricity prices have rose a lot this year.
a: Electricity prices have risen a lot this year.
19.why: Rise – rose – risen: the present perfect needs the past participle.

19.q: I prefer walking to work than to take the bus.
a: I prefer walking to work to taking the bus.
I prefer to walk to work rather than take the bus.
I prefer walking to work rather than taking the bus.
19.why: "Prefer -ing to -ing" or "prefer to do rather than do": keep both forms the same.

19.q: We arrived to the airport two hours early.
a: We arrived at the airport two hours early.
19.why: "Arrive at" a place (building), "arrive in" a city or country, never "arrive to".

19.q: Solar power ____ (become) much cheaper over the last ten years.
a: has become
19.why: "Over the last ten years" → present perfect.

19.q: The factory was so polluting that the city closed it.
a: It was such a polluting factory that the city closed it.
19.why: "Such a + adjective + noun + that" = "so + adjective + that".

20.q: She paid with her phone, what surprised the cashier.
a: She paid with her phone, which surprised the cashier.
20.why: Use ", which" to comment on a whole idea; "what" can't do this.

20.q: I'm not used to pay with cash any more.
a: I'm not used to paying with cash any more.
I'm no longer used to paying with cash.

20.q: The implant is very small and it can be used in a different way.
a: The implant is very small, and it can be used in different ways.
The implant is very small and can be used in different ways.
20.why: "In a different way" is singular; for several, use "in different ways".

20.q: By 2030, millions of people ____ (start) paying with implants.
a: will have started
20.why: Future perfect: completed before a future time.

20.q: Perhaps cash will disappear one day.
a: Cash may disappear one day.
Cash might disappear one day.
Cash could disappear one day.

21.q: Nobody knows where did the first flowers grow.
a: Nobody knows where the first flowers grew.
21.why: In an indirect question, use normal word order (subject + verb), no "did".

21.q: I'm interested to learn more about fossils.
a: I'm interested in learning more about fossils.

21.q: Reading about evolution is more fun than watch documentaries.
a: Reading about evolution is more fun than watching documentaries.
21.why: Compare like with like: -ing form with -ing form.

21.q: The first flowering plants ____ (appear) more than 130 million years ago.
a: appeared

21.q: Some scientists use fossils. Others use DNA.
a: Some scientists use fossils, whereas others use DNA.

22.q: I am using this phone since three years.
a: I have been using this phone for three years.
I have used this phone for three years.
22.why: Up to now → present perfect (continuous); "for" + a period, "since" + a starting point.

22.q: When I listen to music, I feel myself calm.
a: When I listen to music, I feel calm.

22.q: Next year people buy fewer laptops, experts say.
a: Next year people will buy fewer laptops, experts say.
Experts say that people will buy fewer laptops next year.
22.why: A prediction about the future needs "will" (or "be going to").

22.q: If the battery ____ (last) longer, I will keep this phone.
a: lasts
Smartwatches aren't as expensive as smartphones.
22.why: "Not as + adjective + as" is another way to compare.

23.q: Our town has a new solar farm what gives power to 2,000 homes.
a: Our town has a new solar farm which gives power to 2,000 homes.
Our town has a new solar farm that gives power to 2,000 homes.
Our town has a new solar farm, which gives power to 2,000 homes.

23.q: My father use to work in a coal mine.
a: My father used to work in a coal mine.

23.q: Young people spend a lot of money for clothes.
a: Young people spend a lot of money on clothes.

23.q: The number of green jobs ____ (grow) quickly since 2020.
a: has grown

23.q: Workers today need more skills than workers in the past.
a: Workers in the past needed fewer skills than workers today.
23.why: Turning the comparison around: more → fewer (countable).

24.q: Many plants which are not discovered yet may help medicine.
a: Many plants which have not been discovered yet may help medicine.
Many plants that have not been discovered yet may help medicine.
24.why: "Yet" → present perfect; plants don't discover → passive: have not been discovered.

24.q: The forest was more bigger that I imagined.
a: The forest was bigger than I imagined.

24.q: Last summer we have visited three national parks.
a: Last summer we visited three national parks.

24.q: Some trees ____ (disappear) before anyone gives them a name.
a: may disappear
might disappear
could disappear

24.q: Some trees are very tall. Scientists have never found them.
a: Although some trees are very tall, scientists have never found them.
